subtriggers.label: Not enough food earlier
subtriggers.description: Meals or snacks may have been delayed, small, or easy to miss.

subtriggers.label: Medication may be wearing off
subtriggers.description: You have noticed hunger or appetite returning around this medication window.

subtriggers.label: A long gap since eating
subtriggers.description: A long stretch without food can make an urge feel louder and more urgent.

subtriggers.label: Short or disrupted sleep
subtriggers.description: Low sleep can leave the body seeking energy and comfort.

subtriggers.label: Thirst or dry mouth
subtriggers.description: Thirst, dry mouth, and hunger can overlap; both deserve a response.

subtriggers.label: Low energy
subtriggers.description: Your system may be asking for energy, rest, or both.

subtriggers.label: Cycle-related appetite shift
subtriggers.description: You may be in a time when appetite or food preferences naturally change.

subtriggers.label: Stress or pressure
subtriggers.description: Food may feel like a fast route to relief in a loaded moment.

subtriggers.label: Anxious or keyed up
subtriggers.description: Your nervous system may be seeking grounding and predictability.

subtriggers.label: Low, flat, or depleted
subtriggers.description: Pleasure and activation can feel harder to access when mood is low.

subtriggers.label: Lonely or disconnected
subtriggers.description: The urge may be carrying a wish for connection or comfort.

subtriggers.label: Overwhelmed
subtriggers.description: Too many demands can make a quick familiar action feel especially appealing.

subtriggers.label: Celebration or reward
subtriggers.description: A completed task may be cueing a familiar food-reward routine.

subtriggers.label: Food is visible or nearby
subtriggers.description: A cue in your space can pull attention before a conscious decision forms.

subtriggers.label: Someone else is eating
subtriggers.description: Social and visual cues can make an option feel immediately relevant.

subtriggers.label: Screen, ad, or food content
subtriggers.description: Images and routines around screens can prime a food thought.

subtriggers.label: It is the easiest available option
subtriggers.description: Access and convenience shape choices, especially when energy is low.

subtriggers.label: A familiar time of day
subtriggers.description: Your brain may have learned to expect food at this moment.

subtriggers.label: After work, school, or a task
subtriggers.description: Transitions often carry a learned reward or decompression routine.

subtriggers.label: Paired with TV, gaming, or scrolling
subtriggers.description: Two activities can become linked through repetition.

subtriggers.label: Avoiding or delaying a task
subtriggers.description: A food action can create a brief, concrete escape from an unclear task.

subtriggers.label: An automatic route or location
subtriggers.description: A place or sequence may be doing much of the cueing.

subtriggers.label: A very specific sensory need
subtriggers.description: The exact texture, flavor, or temperature may matter more than the food category.

subtriggers.label: Need to chew, sip, or keep the mouth busy
subtriggers.description: Your system may be seeking oral movement or steady stimulation.

subtriggers.label: Temperature or texture comfort
subtriggers.description: Warmth, cold, crunch, softness, or creaminess may be regulating.

subtriggers.label: Bored or understimulated
subtriggers.description: Your attention system may be looking for novelty, movement, or intensity.
